title: Pars IV opens: Rome next claims unwritten tradition equals Scripture
source_text: I. THESIBUS novissimis solvimus argumenta, quibus Pontificii ostendere se putant Scripturam non esse plenam & sufficientem fidei regulam. Sequitur ut ea solvamus quibus probare conantur traditiones non scriptas aequalem cum Scriptura sacra authoritatem habere, & pari pietatis affectu esse suscipiendas.
pass_a_gloss: By the newest theses we have solved the arguments by which the Pontificians think they show that Scripture is not a full and sufficient rule of faith. It follows that we solve those by which they try to prove that unwritten traditions have equal authority with sacred Scripture, and are to be received with equal affection of piety.
pass_b_english: Pars III answered the claim that Scripture is not a full faith-rule.
Pars IV turns to Rome next move: unwritten traditions share Scripture authority.
They want those traditions received with the same piety as the written word.
We take up that equal-authority claim thesis by thesis.

choices.term: aequalem cum Scriptura sacra authoritatem habere
choices.english: to have equal authority with sacred Scripture
choices.why: States the Pars IV target claim cleanly.
